title: Common synthetic point-in-time baseline framework
objective: Implement a replaceable, point-in-time-safe synthetic framework that evaluates incumbent, random, transparent-rule, recency, and simple statistical ranking policies on identical candidate/route-day inputs and outcome contracts without claiming predictive validity or incremental lift.
business_reason: A complex model has no defensible value unless it beats meaningful simple baselines under one leakage-resistant evaluator; this is the next depth-first consumer of the hardened outcome boundary and the prerequisite for calibration and economics.
inputs: OUTCOMES-001 frozen common-as-of labels and claim ceiling
synthetic point-in-time features and splits only
non_goals: tune on future or outcome-derived information
ingest real source or CRM data
evaluator: freeze a common public evaluator contract before material implementation
one exact point-in-time feature/label/split interface for every baseline
deterministic ranking, exact-ten/abstain, metric, replacement, and complexity rules
registered leakage, missing-baseline, unfair-comparison, nondeterminism, and overclaim mutations
known_bad_cases: future feature admitted to a historical decision
different candidate sets or splits used across policies
random baseline is unseeded or non-replayable
complex model declared superior without registered replacement margin
synthetic metric represented as predictive validity or lift
exact-ten/protection invariant bypassed by a baseline
acceptance: incumbent, seeded random, transparent rule, recency, and simple statistical policies share one strict interface and identical synthetic evaluation inputs
features obey event/recorded/available/decision clocks and labels obey OUTCOMES maturity semantics
every policy produces exactly ten distinct eligible physical locations or ABSTAIN_NO_VALID_TEN through the existing MATH contract
metrics, uncertainty placeholders, replacement rules, and complexity penalties are frozen before candidate implementation
all registered mutations are rejected and independent sweeps find no surviving leakage or comparison asymmetry
all real predictive, causal, commercial, and production claims remain behind named gates
rollback: Remove the baseline framework and retain the validated OUTCOMES-001/MATH-001 interfaces; invalidate dependent calibration/economics fixtures and keep all real-use permissions disabled.
stop_budget: Remain synthetic and non-influencing; do not use real source rows, infer predictive validity, tune on unavailable outcomes, authorize live ranking, or convert empirical uncertainty into assumptions.
